system: You rewrite research decisions as topic-neutral abstractions. Return only the JSON object asked for.
prompt:
Below are research decisions made by several different researchers. Rewrite each one into the fixed
template below so that a reader cannot tell what field, topic, paper, organisation or person it comes from, nor what
kind of work it is: an experiment, a new procedure, a measurement suite, a write-up choice, or a decision about what
to share or fund must all read alike. Keep the trade-off that was faced and which way it was decided.

Template, one entry per item:
- "situation": one sentence, at most 30 words: the position the researcher was in when the decision came up.
- "options_considered": two or three short options separated by " / ", including the one taken. If the source names
  no alternative, give the plain opposite of what was done.
- "choice": one sentence, at most 25 words, starting with "Chose", saying which option was taken.
- "reason": one sentence, at most 25 words, giving the stated reason; if none is stated write "No reason stated."

Rules:
- Remove every domain noun and technical term: names of models, systems, datasets, procedures, organisations, people,
  papers and coined terms; and any wording that reveals the area.
- Use only plain generic words such as: the result, the claim, the finding, the check, the comparison, the setup,
  the change, the next step, the question, the work, the variant, the condition, the sample, the system.
- Never use any of these words or any form of them: ability, access, accuracy, allow, appeared, assessment, attack, avoid, baselines, behavior, behaviour, benchmark, best, bound, call, capability, cheap, claiming, clean, comes, complex, components, content, cost, defense, difficulty, disclosure, effect, effects, error, evaluate, evaluated, evaluating, evaluation, evaluator, evaluators, failures, features, form, format, four, gains, generalise, generalization, generalize, ground, harm, harmful, implication, improve, improvement, information, internal, intervention, judged, key, limit, matched, mechanism, method, methods, metric, observed, organisation, pattern, performance, phenomenon, picture, point, policy, possibly, practical, preference, preferences, public, publication, publish, rater, reduce, release, residual, responses, risk, rule, safety, sampled, say, score, shifts, similar, source, stage, success, supporting, task, tasks, technique, time, tool, tools, trait, transfer, transferred, treatment, unintended, unmodified, unwanted, value, varies, verify, wording.
- Add nothing that is not in the source. Never say who made the decision. Write every item in the same plain style.
- Some items list "forbidden_terms": words a previous rewrite kept. Use none of them nor any synonym or form of
  them.
Return {"items": [{"id": ..., "situation": ..., "options_considered": ..., "choice": ..., "reason": ...}, ...]}
with one entry per input item, in input order.

ITEMS:
[
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:6c8d92959e02",
  "problem": "How to choose inoculation prompts without running an expensive fine-tune for every candidate.",
  "did": "They proposed and validated a heuristic: select the prompt that best elicits the undesired behavior from the initial model, testing the correlation with IP effectiveness across settings.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "training with every candidate prompt"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Prompts that more strongly elicit the behavior before fine-tuning inoculate more effectively, and elicitation can be measured without a training run.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "train",
   "training",
   "trigger"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:306deb4d7f2b",
  "problem": "How to handle disclosure for ML attacks in 2018 when the field had no disclosure policies and few deployed models.",
  "did": "Only notified the model authors and checked for errors in the papers before publishing the attacks immediately.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "performing some kind of responsible disclosure"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Almost nobody used machine learning models in 2018, so a responsible disclosure process would offer little benefit.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "norm",
   "user"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:cf4362ff260d",
  "problem": "Whether fine-tuning damage explains the observed CoT override",
  "did": "Rejected capability degradation as a sufficient explanation, citing retained GPQA Diamond performance and CoT-following when the same persona answers.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "fine-tuning degrading thinking capabilities"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Both DeepSeek finetunes kept their GPQA Diamond capabilities and still follow their CoT when they answer with the same persona.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "override",
   "persona",
   "reasoning",
   "training"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:1343b05c7a7b",
  "problem": "How strongly to state the claim that diverse training improves AOs given that gains vary across models and tasks.",
  "did": "They claimed consistent improvement from scaling the mixture while qualifying that the value of diversity is model- and task-dependent, with SPQA-only already competitive on some secret-keeping tasks.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "On Gemma/Llama secret-keeping SPQA-only is within error of white-box baselines, whereas on Qwen3-8B tasks scaling yields much larger improvements.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "diverse",
   "training"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "jacob_steinhardt:2e044ca68cad",
  "problem": "Choosing a fair comparison between the decoder's activation-based steering and RepE, which offers two control variants.",
  "did": "They used RepE's training-based LoRRA finetuning variant rather than its training-free steering vector method for the debiasing comparison.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "RepE training-free method that adds steering vectors to activations"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "For a fair comparison.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "fine",
   "free",
   "training"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:33e06b823cb3",
  "problem": "How to measure whether introspection adapters actually help auditors find hidden behaviors on AuditBench.",
  "did": "They used the benchmark's standard investigator agent success rate, with 16 runs per model and an LLM classifier on 10 predictions, for direct comparison with prior tools, and used raw verbalization rates only as corroboration.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "raw verbalization rate"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Success rate allows direct comparison with prior auditing techniques; raw verbalization rates only measure true positive rate and don't reflect whether a behavior would be surfaced in practice.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "agent",
   "component",
   "hidden",
   "investigating"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "nicholas_carlini:4f7604004e3e",
  "problem": "Whether to require the LLM to produce working proof-of-concept exploits for the Chrome extension vulnerabilities.",
  "did": "They dropped automated exploit generation and instead manually validated each of the 54 flagged cases themselves.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "having the model develop proof-of-concept exploits"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Models could not complete validation, which requires real-world actions like creating accounts that LLMs refuse or are slow at.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "performs",
   "production"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:ccf98c6ef284",
  "problem": "How to test a targeted phishing task realistically without causing real harm.",
  "did": "They used a volunteer student as a dummy victim, intercepted outgoing emails, simulated the victim's responses, and kept all steps under human oversight without putting websites online.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "letting agents send emails outside the organization",
   "putting websites online"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Safety: avoiding real phishing of outside parties while still testing the end-to-end task.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "agent",
   "deception",
   "human"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "samuel_marks:7343b4e136c8",
  "problem": "How to evaluate whether activation verbalizers generalize to practically relevant tasks far from their training distribution, and compare against other methods.",
  "did": "They evaluated AOs on downstream auditing tasks (secret-keeping, emergent misalignment) where activations come from fine-tuned models never seen in training and prior white- and black-box baselines exist.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "narrow evaluations such as held-out SAE features or user attributes"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "Prior evaluations were narrow and did not study generalization to very different tasks where LatentQA decoders could be compared to baseline methods.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "auditing",
   "decoding",
   "downstream",
   "training"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "owain_evans:daa960395c70",
  "problem": "Which proxies to study in place of real misalignment such as reward seeking and secret loyalties",
  "did": "Studied capabilities, backdoors and narrow reward hacking in chess, not the misalignment forms themselves.",
  "alternatives_named": [
   "reward seeking",
   "scheming",
   "secret loyalties"
  ],
  "stated_reason": "The real forms of misalignment are difficult to elicit and measure reliably. The proxies can be measured directly and constructed to be absent from the base model.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "forms",
   "themselve"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:a5de72a613c6",
  "problem": "How much to trust informal forecasts as a substitute for baselines, given that 79 tasks rely on them.",
  "did": "They compared forecasts to successful baseline times, found R^2=0.51, and concluded forecasts are a reasonable proxy but that baselines still add substantial information.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "The moderate correlation indicates forecasts are informative but leave considerable unexplained variance.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "times"
  ]
 },
 {
  "id": "elizabeth_barnes:1a505b6214cb",
  "problem": "How strongly to state conclusions about casual users' ability to reach the ARA threshold.",
  "did": "They stated a conclusion scoped to casual users without fine-tuning access and to the specific model versions tested.",
  "alternatives_named": [],
  "stated_reason": "Their agents were limited and fine-tuning could change capabilities, so the claim is conditional.",
  "forbidden_terms": [
   "agent",
   "training"
  ]
 }
]

{"items": [
{"id": "samuel_marks:6c8d92959e02", "situation": "A candidate input had to be picked for a procedure, and trying every candidate in full was expensive.", "options_considered": "Pick the candidate using a quick pre-check on the starting system / try every candidate in a full run", "choice": "Chose to pick the candidate using the quick pre-check on the starting system.", "reason": "Candidates that more strongly produce the target outcome at the start work better later, and that can be measured without a full run."},
{"id": "nicholas_carlini:306deb4d7f2b", "situation": "Findings about weaknesses in systems were ready, but the field had no agreed sharing practices and very few systems were in use.", "options_considered": "Notify only the owners, check for mistakes, then share immediately / run a staged, delayed sharing process", "choice": "Chose to notify only the owners, check for mistakes, and share the findings immediately.", "reason": "Almost nothing was in use then, so a staged sharing process would offer little benefit."},
{"id": "owain_evans:cf4362ff260d", "situation": "An odd outcome was seen after an earlier adjustment to the system, and it was unclear whether damage from that adjustment explained it.", "options_considered": "Accept that the adjustment damaged the system's competence / reject damage as a sufficient explanation", "choice": "Chose to reject damage as a sufficient explanation for the outcome.", "reason": "Both adjusted variants kept their earlier test strength and still follow their own stated steps under the same condition."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:1343b05c7a7b", "situation": "A claim that broader variety helps had to be worded, though the benefit differs across systems and settings.", "options_considered": "State consistent help without qualification / state consistent help while noting the size depends on system and setting", "choice": "Chose to state consistent help while noting that the size of the benefit depends on system and setting.", "reason": "In some settings the simple variant was already within noise of the comparison options, while in another the larger set gave much bigger boosts."},
{"id": "jacob_steinhardt:2e044ca68cad", "situation": "A fair comparison was needed against another approach that offers two variants of control.", "options_considered": "Use the variant with an extra optimization step / use the variant needing no extra optimization step", "choice": "Chose the variant that involves an extra optimization step.", "reason": "For a fair comparison."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:33e06b823cb3", "situation": "A way was needed to measure whether a new addition helps investigators uncover concealed quirks in systems.", "options_considered": "Use the standard rate of right answers from investigators / use the raw rate at which the system states the quirk", "choice": "Chose the standard rate of right answers, using raw rates only as corroboration.", "reason": "It permits direct comparison with earlier approaches, while raw rates only capture true positives and don't show whether a quirk would be surfaced in real use."},
{"id": "nicholas_carlini:4f7604004e3e", "situation": "Flagged weaknesses needed confirming, and the question was whether the system should produce working demonstrations for each.", "options_considered": "Have the system build working demonstrations / check each flagged case by hand", "choice": "Chose to drop automated demonstrations and check every flagged case by hand.", "reason": "The system could not complete the check, which needs real-world steps such as creating accounts that it refuses or does slowly."},
{"id": "elizabeth_barnes:ccf98c6ef284", "situation": "A targeted deceptive-message scenario had to be tested realistically without causing real damage to anyone.", "options_considered": "Let systems message outsiders and put sites online / use a volunteer stand-in target with intercepted messages and simulated replies under close supervision", "choice": "Chose the volunteer stand-in target, intercepted messages, simulated replies and close supervision, with no sites put online.", "reason": "Protect outside parties from real targeting while still testing the full sequence from start to finish."},
{"id": "samuel_marks:7343b4e136c8", "situation": "It was unclear whether a method works in far-off settings, and a comparison with other options was also wanted.", "options_considered": "Test on narrow checks / test on varied real-use settings with altered systems never seen before and existing comparison options", "choice": "Chose to test on varied real-use settings with altered systems never seen before, where comparison options already exist.", "reason": "Earlier checks were narrow and did not study very different settings where the approach could be compared with other options."},
{"id": "owain_evans:daa960395c70", "situation": "Stand-ins had to be picked for real problems that are hard to study.", "options_considered": "Study the real problems directly / study measurable stand-ins", "choice": "Chose to study measurable stand-ins instead of the real problems.", "reason": "The real problems are hard to produce and measure reliably, while stand-ins can be measured directly and built to be absent from the starting system."},
{"id": "elizabeth_barnes:a5de72a613c6", "situation": "Many items relied on informal estimates in place of measured reference results, and the question was how far to trust them.", "options_considered": "Treat estimates as sufficient / treat them as a reasonable stand-in but keep the measured references", "choice": "Chose to treat estimates as a reasonable stand-in while stating that measured references still add a lot.", "reason": "The moderate correlation shows estimates are informative but leave considerable unexplained variance."},
{"id": "elizabeth_barnes:1a505b6214cb", "situation": "A conclusion about whether casual people could reach a threshold had to be worded.", "options_considered": "State a broad conclusion / state a conclusion scoped to casual people and the specific versions tested", "choice": "Chose a conclusion scoped to casual people without the option to adjust the system and to the specific versions tested.", "reason": "The systems tested were weak and later adjustment could change what they can do, so the claim is conditional."}
]}
